data.title: Memory-Dump and Forensic-Acquisition Evasion
data.summary: The sample actively resists memory acquisition: it overwrites decrypted code and strings immediately after use, locks or re-encrypts sensitive regions, or detects a dump attempt and terminates before it completes.
data.description:
Unlike packing, which protects the file on disk, this protects the process while it runs:
sensitive buffers are zeroed or re-encrypted the moment they are no longer needed, so a
memory snapshot taken even seconds later shows nothing useful. Some samples go further and
monitor for the API calls a memory-acquisition tool makes (MiniDumpWriteDump, process
handle duplication with full access) and self-terminate or corrupt their own image when
they see one.
data.recommendation:
* Capture memory at the specific moment of use (breakpoint on decryption, not a time-delayed snapshot) rather than after the fact.
* Hook or neutralise the self-termination trigger before attempting acquisition, and verify the dump is complete and uncorrupted.
* Treat an empty or garbage result from a standard dump as evidence of this behaviour, not as an unprotected sample with nothing to find.
data.short_recommendation: Capture memory at the moment of use via a breakpoint rather than a delayed snapshot.

mitre_techniques.procedure: A delayed memory snapshot returned zeroed buffers where a breakpoint-timed capture showed decrypted content.

mbc_techniques.implementation: Decrypted buffers were zeroed immediately after use, defeating a delayed memory snapshot.
